subject: Request: Regional maintenance carve-out & monthly credit calculation
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cloudhaven.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: regional maintenance carve-out & monthly credit calculation

Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Two quick asks so we can move the contract review forward with procurement and finance:

1) Regional maintenance carve-out: CloudHaven runs a quarterly network maintenance in us-west that can cause short regional unavailability for background batching. We need a temporary carve-out described in the SLA that excludes these scheduled maintenance windows from uptime calculations for the first 6 months of the term. Can you confirm you can accept a clause that references: "scheduled regional maintenance windows (announced >=72 hours) for up to 6 hours per calendar month, for a maximum of 3 months in the initial 6-month pilot"?

2) Monthly credit calculation: Redwood typically pro-rates credits against the month’s invoice when an uptime breach is detected. For this account CloudHaven has requested a fixed-monthly credit bucket instead of per-incident pro-rates (simpler for their accounting). We can offer a capped monthly credit pool but need to align on the formula. Proposal below:

  - Baseline uptime: 99.95% per region (standard in our hosted offering)
  - Credit ladder: 99.95–99.90 => 5% of monthly committed spend; 99.90–99.80 => 10%; <99.80 => 20% (capped at 40% per month)
  - Credit pool: apply the calculated percent to the smaller of (i) monthly committed invoice, or (ii) $50k (to cap exposure)

Can you confirm CloudHaven’s tolerance for the regional maintenance carve-out language and the monthly credit mechanics? If you want to trade the 6-month carve-out for a slightly higher credit cap we can discuss.

I’ve attached the current SLA amendment (SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf) with inline placeholders for the carve-out.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf (pdf, 74KB)
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cloudhaven.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@cloudhaven.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: regional maintenance carve-out & monthly credit calculation

Sean —

Appreciate the clear proposal and the worksheet you sent. Quick answers:

1) Maintenance carve-out: CloudHaven can accept a scheduled maintenance carve-out but we need it limited to announced maintenance only (no implied unannounced). The 72-hour notice is fine. Two asks:
  - Please make the carve-out explicitly regional (i.e., only affects the affected region’s uptime calculation).
  - Exclude any maintenance that affects customer-facing control plane APIs (we need those to remain in uptime metrics).

2) Monthly credit calculation: The fixed monthly pool is attractive—our finance team prefers deterministic crediting. We would push to increase the cap from $50k to $75k for the pilot months only (months 1–3). After month 3 revert to $50k.

Counterproposal:
  - Keep baseline 99.95%.
  - For pilot months (1–3): cap = $75k; after pilot cap = $50k.
  - Credit ladder as you proposed but remove the 40% hard cap; instead use a per-month cap equal to the monthly cap above (i.e., credit <= cap value).

I’m attaching a redline and will loop in contracts for the exact language. If you can accept the pilot cap bump we’ll be happy to sign quickly.

Best,
Alex Turner
Director of Infrastructure, CloudHaven
alex.turner@cloudhaven.com

Attachment: CH_SLA_Redline_20270517.docx (Word, 45KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cloudhaven.com>, contracts@cloudhaven.com
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: regional maintenance carve-out & monthly credit calculation

Alex / contracts team —

Thanks for the quick review and the redline. A few clarifications from Redwood’s side to keep procurement moving:

- Regional carve-out language: we will tighten the wording so it only applies to non-control-plane maintenance in the affected region. Proposed phrasing: "Scheduled regional maintenance windows, which are communicated to the customer at least 72 hours in advance and which do not impact control plane APIs, will be excluded from the calculation of regional uptime for the period specified in this amendment."

- Pilot cap trade: Redwood can accept a temporary pilot cap increase to $75k for months 1–3, provided CloudHaven accepts a reduction back to $50k for months 4–6 and a review meeting at the end of month 3 to evaluate impact. This protects both parties.

- Credit cap mechanics: we cannot remove a % cap entirely (finance needs the exposure quantified). Compromise: keep your per-month dollar cap (pilot/standard) and also keep a 40% percent-of-month cap as a secondary safeguard — whichever is lower applies. That prevents pathological cases where the percent would exceed practical exposure.

If that sounds reasonable, Ben can update the amendment and circulate v3 for signatures. Suggested next steps: Ben to produce SLA_Amendment_v3.pdf with updated carve-out and cap language; we’ll send to your contracts for routing to DocuSign.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0133

Alex / contracts —

Appreciate the flexibility. We incorporated Marissa’s compromise and produced SLA_Amendment_v3.pdf (attached) with:

- Explicit regional carve-out limited to non-control-plane scheduled maintenance communicated >=72 hours in advance.
- Pilot cap = $75k months 1–3; standard cap = $50k months 4–6.
- Credit ladder unchanged. Final cap applied = min(dollar cap, 40% of monthly committed spend).

Ben summary of calculations (example): if monthly committed spend = $120k and region drops to 99.85% => ladder => 10% => theoretical credit = $12k, applied cap = min($75k, 0.4 * $120k = $48k) => final credit = $12k.

Please confirm acceptance by replying "ACK and route to DocuSign" and we’ll send the DocuSign packet for signatures.

Thanks — Ben
